description: Community-led foresight centers affected knowledge and local climate risk experience.
Co-governance gives affected people recurring authority and decision pathways.
Sovereignty stewardship cultural continuity and land relationships shape future-making.
Technology assessment panels surface rights risks access barriers and lived impacts before deployment.
Sortition and balanced design improve representation but still require institutional uptake.
Participatory budgeting improves decision access when budget shares are meaningful.
Youth councils surface long-term stakes but can become symbolic without response duties.
Digital platforms scale participation but risk underrepresenting digitally excluded groups.
Open comment processes reach some publics but underrepresent people with time access and trust barriers.
